To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

stalking following the breakup of heterosexual romantic relationships was more likely in participants whose former partners had a history of substance misuse, criminal involvement, violence, mental health problems, relationship difficulties, reacting with inappropriate emotion (e.g. jealousy), and suspiciousness of participants' relationships with others.

stalking following the breakup of relationships is associated with the former partner having: a history of alcohol and/or drug use; criminal involvement; violence, mental health problems; relationship difficulties; reacting with inappropriate emotions; and jealousy and suspicious attitudes toward the participant's relationships.

stalking victims were more likely to have had a former partner who had substance abuse problems, criminal involvement, violence, mental health problems, difficulties in forming relationships, and who reacted with inappropriate emotion and jealous and suspiciousness of their relationships with others.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of those characteristics of former intimate partners that are associated with stalking as a post-relationship experience of harassment.
the identification and understanding of stalking behavior in the context of romantic relationships.
the identification of characteristics of former partners who stalk following the dissolution of relationships.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

stalking former partners following the breakup of heterosexual romantic relationships is more likely to occur if the former partner has a history of violence, mental health problems, substance use, and difficulties in forming relationships.

stalking is a form of harassment which occurs when the stalker has a history of substance abuse, criminal involvement, violence, mental health problems, difficulty forming relationships, reacting with inappropriate emotions, jealousy, and suspiciousness of others, and the victim has a history of victimization, low self-esteem, and poor social support.
the characteristics of stalking former partner's are: a history of violence, mental health problems, substance use and difficulties in forming relationships.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

stalking is a serious and potentially life threatening crime that is perpetrated primarily by men, and primarily against women, and that stalking is a crime that is often associated with a history of violence and abuse in the relationship.
stalking is a complex behavior that is associated with a range of factors that may be related to attachment problems, personality problems, and psychosocial problems.

stalking following the breakup of a romantic relationship is more likely when the former partner: has a history of violence; substance use; criminal involvement; mental health problems and relationship problems; reacts with jealousy, suspiciousness and inappropriate emotion; is male; and is the participant's first romantic relationship.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vast majority of people who have been involved in a relationship that ended badly will not be stalked, and the vast majority of stalkers will not be violent.
the majority of stalking victims are women and that stalking is not a rare phenomenon.
stalking is a complex and serious form of harassment that is associated with many negative outcomes for the victims.
